protocol: manual semantic review; exact-string overlap is reported separately and is not a quality score
must_not_policy: A violation is recorded separately from must coverage; unsupported claims of checks are called out in rationale.

before.rationale: Names the shared package, public import, and search, but gives no concrete checkout/export evidence and invents helper names and behavior.

after.rationale: Names the owning source and public index paths, explains the package boundary, and keeps the import at the public entrypoint.

before.rationale: Correctly requests the missing procedure and names mcp.ts/root.ts, but cannot inspect the owner or state the live boundary without that identifier.

after.rationale: Same underspecification is handled safely; it asks for the procedure and describes the source paths without claiming a live result.

before.rationale: Invents a generic review and verdict, with no actual diff, check, changed paths, or limitation.

after.rationale: Refuses to invent a completed review, names the narrow boundary to inspect, and states no diff/checks were available; it still does not run a focused check.

before.rationale: Covers hidden semantics, page discovery, adjacent typed patterns, and the omission of an obvious control tour.

after.rationale: Covers hidden semantics and avoids a tour, but asserts a generic advanced page and placeholder setting instead of identifying the concrete feature page.

before.rationale: Applies the reader-value test and leaves docs unchanged.

after.rationale: Leaves docs unchanged and correctly limits a possible label update to an existing reference.

must_not_violations: claims a docs build/link proof succeeded without evidence
before.rationale: Lists the expected page and checks, but reports a successful full build/link proof despite no actual run or concrete contract details.

after.rationale: Separates source inspection and formatting from the explicitly unrun build/link proof; the page and contract remain placeholders and only formatting is claimed run.

before.rationale: Preserves protected auth, bounds limit, describes scope/IDs, eagerly registers the router, and names the focused extraction check; no service list is specified by the synthetic task.

after.rationale: Same safe exposure shape with concrete paths, bounded input, stable IDs, eager registration, and focused-check evidence; supported services remain unspecified.

before.rationale: Correctly refuses exposure, preserves server-owned encryption/non-return requirements, and calls for security review when auth/audit is unclear.

after.rationale: Maintains the same sensitive-flow refusal and explicitly keeps raw credentials out of inputs and descriptions.

before.rationale: Uses full permission, states irreversible deletion and the ID source, bounds id, and calls the extraction check; focused schema/authorization checks are only described.

after.rationale: Names the procedure/tool, retains full permission, describes the destructive effect and ID source, shows bounded schema, and labels source/focused checks versus live proof.

before.rationale: Correctly says eager mcp.ts registration is required, but omits generated name/description/schema inspection and an explicit live-call-unverified label.

after.rationale: Still correctly rejects metadata-only exposure but does not provide the generated tool surface or explicitly label a live transport check unverified.
